column1: # HES97 (a) (the user, 2026-11-17; built by hs-speed, 2026-11-22): the programs of hsi's run corpora whose run needs more than the
# check's 60 s of CPU, with their own CPU limit (bin/lib/hsi/check's HSI_CPU_CAPS; GHC's testsuite's run_timeout_multiplier):
# ID<TAB>SECONDS<TAB>CPU, the cap about 1.5 times the CPU seconds (user + system, every thread) hsi took on the main host (amd64)
# (hs-speed's measurement, 2026-11-22: CPU the user + system seconds of a run at a 600 s limit, 4 jobs; the cap 1.5 times the larger of
# that and the wall seconds of an earlier run at 4 jobs on a host loaded 90 to 140 on 64 cores, rounded up to 10 s)
# hs-pkgs-1122 (2026-11-22): nofib's parallel programs GHC builds with the Hackage packages, measured the same way (a run at a 600 s
# limit through a timing wrapper, 3 jobs; their earlier runs were killed at 60 s, so the cap 1.5 times the CPU, rounded up to 10 s);
# mandel, parfib and secretary met the 600 s and have none
# hs-pkgs-1122 (2026-11-22, hs-pkgs-2): eff's VSD and VSM and hartel's solid the same way (a 600 s run, 4 jobs; the cap 1.5 times the
# CPU); eff/VS ran out of the light runs' 8 GiB at 85 s of CPU and has none until a run at the check's 16 GiB
# smalls-1123 (2026-11-23): eff/VS at the check's 16 GiB under the big-job lock, the same way (a 600 s run, 1 job: 96.4 s of CPU, passing)
